record.paper_title: Selected Old Open Problems in General Topology
record.original_question: Does there exist, in ZFC, a countably compact topological group G whose square G × G fails to be countably compact?

evidence.quote:
Problem 12. Construct in ZF C a countably compact topological group G such that
its square G × G is not countably compact.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Work in ZFC (Zermelo–Fraenkel set theory with the Axiom of Choice). A topological space X is called countably compact if every countable open cover of X has a finite subcover (equivalently, every infinite subset of X has an accumulation point in X). A topological group is a group G equipped with a topology such that the multiplication map G × G → G and the inversion map G → G are continuous.

Does there exist, provably in ZFC, a countably compact topological group G such that the product space G × G is not countably compact?
artifact.status_search_result: Constructions of a countably compact group with non-countably-compact square are known under additional set-theoretic assumptions (e.g., MA, CH, or the existence of selective ultrafilters). In ZFC, Hrušák, van Mill, Ramos-García and Shelah (2021) constructed two countably compact groups whose product is not countably compact, and Bardyla–Ravsky–Zdomskyy obtained a ZFC example whose square is not countably pracompact only under MA. The original problem of constructing in ZFC a single countably compact group whose square fails to be countably compact does not appear to be resolved.

status_evidence.title: Countably compact groups without non-trivial convergent sequences
status_evidence.snippet: Construction in ZFC of two countably compact groups whose product is not countably compact (via a countably compact subgroup of 2^c without nontrivial convergent sequences).
status_evidence.claim: In ZFC there exist two countably compact groups whose product is not countably compact, but the single-group square version is not addressed.

status_evidence.title: A countably compact topological group with the non-countably pracompact square
status_evidence.snippet: Under MA, a Boolean countably compact topological group whose square is not countably pracompact is constructed.
status_evidence.claim: Constructions of countably compact groups with non-countably-compact square still rely on extra axioms such as MA.

status_evidence.title: On powers of countably pracompact groups
status_evidence.snippet: Discusses constructions of countably compact groups whose powers fail countable compactness, generally under additional set-theoretic hypotheses.
status_evidence.claim: The ZFC version for a single group's square remains a recognized open problem.
